learning_outcomes.text: Knows and understands the importance of physics as a natural science, its place and role in today's science and technology, especially the importance of solid-state physics for applications in electrical engineering and electronics; perceives the mutual relations between theory and experiment.
Has up-to-date knowledge in the field of modern physics, knows the current state of research, follows the development of physics.

Has knowledge in the field of electricity and magnetism, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, optics, interaction of radiation with matter, and modern physics, necessary to understand basic physical phenomena in nature and technology, and in particular in electrical engineering and electronics.
Can apply appropriate physical laws and principles to solve problems in electromagnetism and quantum mechanics.
Acquires the ability to plan and conduct measurements of physical quantities.
Possesses the practical ability to analyze measurement results, prepare reports, and analyze the uncertainty of results.
Possesses the practical ability to analyze measurement results, prepare reports, and analyze the uncertainty of results.
Perceives the necessity of developing practical skills in describing physical phenomena.
Working in a group, the student perceives the need for cooperation in performing laboratory tasks and jointly bearing responsibility for developing and presenting the results of their work.
Based on acquired practical skills, the student can undertake actions to plan and implement new experiments, e.g., in the field of electrical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Maxwell's equations: Maxwell's correction to Ampere's law. Ampere-Maxwell law in integral and differential form. Real current vs. displacement current. Continuity of current in a circuit containing a capacitor. Maxwell's equations in integral and differential form.

Physical pendulums: Purpose of the exercise: To become familiar with the oscillating motion of a physical pendulum. Determination of the moment of inertia of rigid bodies by measuring the period of oscillation and based on geometric dimensions.
Free fall: Purpose of the exercise: Observation of free fall using electronic recording of the ball's flight time through measurement points. Determination of gravitational acceleration.

Electromagnetic waves, wave optics: Generation and propagation of electromagnetic waves, electromagnetic wave equation, energy transport by electromagnetic waves. Young's experiment, light interference, coherence of light waves. Light diffraction. Diffraction. Diffraction from a single slit, interference from multiple slits, diffraction gratings and their applications, X-ray diffraction. Light polarization, linear polarization, generation of polarized light.
Young's modulus: Purpose of the exercise: Determination of Young's modulus by the static method through measurement of the elongation of a wire of the tested metal loaded with a constant force.
Viscosity coefficient: Purpose of the exercise: To become familiar with the properties of a viscous liquid, determine the viscosity coefficient using the falling ball method (Stokes' method).
Light and quantum physics: Thermal radiation, spectral distribution of radiation, Stefan-Boltzmann law, Planck's hypothesis. External photoelectric effect. Compton effect.
Semiconductor diode: Purpose of the exercise: To understand the properties of layered p-n semiconductor junctions. Determination and analysis of DC characteristics for various types of diodes.

Atomic structure and matter waves: Atomic and molecular spectra. Bohr model of the hydrogen atom. Energy states and spectrum of the hydrogen atom. Corpuscular-wave structure of matter, de Broglie hypothesis, Davisson-Germer experiment, de Broglie waves.
Refractive index of solids: Purpose of the exercise: Determination of the refractive index of solids by measuring the apparent thickness of a plate using a microscope.

Elements of quantum mechanics: Wave function, Schroedinger equation, uncertainty principle, Schroedinger theory of the hydrogen atom, interpretation of the wave function, quantization of physical quantities, quantum numbers. Orbital angular momentum and electron spin, Pauli's exclusion principle, periodic table of elements, X-rays, lasers.

Lenses: Purpose of the exercise: Measurement of focal lengths of a converging lens and a lens system (converging and diverging), calculation of the focal length of a diverging lens. Observation and measurement of optical aberration defects. Measurement of the focal length of eyeglass lenses and an objective lens.

Condensed matter: Types of crystals (types of bonds), energy levels and bands, metals and semiconductors, doped semiconductors, applications of semiconductors, magnetic properties of matter. New materials in modern technology.

Light diffraction from single and double slits: Purpose of the exercise: Measurement of light intensity in the diffraction pattern of a single slit and a system of two slits. Determination of slit size.
Nuclear physics: Atomic nucleus structure, nucleon-nucleon interaction, nuclear decays, nuclear reactions, interaction of ionizing radiation with matter.
Energy gap in germanium: Purpose of the exercise: Determination of the energy gap width by measuring the temperature dependence of the resistance of a germanium monocrystal.
Evolution of the universe, introduction to the standard model.
Polarimeter: Purpose of the exercise: Measurement of the angle of rotation of the polarization plane in sugar solutions.
Electrolysis: Purpose of the exercise: Determination of the electrochemical equivalent of copper and Faraday's constant in an experiment with electrolysis of an aqueous CuSO4 solution.

Gamma radiation dosimetry: Purpose of the exercise: To become familiar with the basics of ionizing radiation dosimetry. Comparison of the absorption properties of gamma radiation by various materials.

Photoelectric effect: Purpose of the exercise: Observation of the photoelectric effect: electron emission from metal by light of different frequencies (colors). Measurement of the kinetic energy of emitted electrons allows calculation of Planck's constant and the work function of electrons.

Electrostatic field modeling: Purpose of the exercise: To understand the basic quantities describing the electrostatic field. Determination of equipotential surfaces and electric field intensity vectors in a plane for various electrode configurations.

Interference of acoustic waves: Purpose of the exercise: Determination of the speed of sound in gases by the acoustic wave interference method, using a Quincke tube. Determination of Cp/CV for the tested gases.
Malus's Law: Purpose of the exercise: To become familiar with the phenomenon of visible light polarization and to verify Malus's law.

Wheatstone bridge: Purpose of the exercise: Wheatstone bridge as an example of applying Kirchhoff's laws to describe complex electrical circuits. Measurement of unknown resistances and their series and parallel connections.

Capacitors: Purpose of the exercise: Measurement of the capacitance of air capacitors and capacitors with a dielectric layer to determine the electric constant ε0 and the relative permittivity εr of various materials.

Tangent compass: Purpose of the exercise: To become familiar with the construction and operation of an instrument called a tangent compass. Determination of the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field.

Electromagnetic oscillations of the LCR circuit: Purpose of the exercise: Observation of damped oscillations and aperiodic waveforms in an LCR circuit. Measurement and interpretation of parameters describing the observed voltage waveforms U(t).

Resistance thermometer and thermocouple: Purpose of the exercise: Determination of the temperature coefficient of platinum resistance. Measurement of the characteristic of a copper-constantan thermocouple.
assessment_rules: Only students with a positive grade (at least 3.0) from laboratory classes are admitted to the exam. The exam is conducted in three terms. Students perform laboratory exercises according to the materials provided by the instructor. Students are obliged to prepare for the performed exercise, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Passing the classes is based on presenting a solution to the posed problem. Passing the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes.
